text:
maria: Quick follow-up from the lazy-reserve RFC — thinking out loud about adding a lightweight `lazy_reserve` state to the allocator to avoid eagerly backing small micro-batch pages. goal: reduce early pin churn + fragmentation for short-lived tensors while keeping re-fault latency predictable. cc @alex @tomas :thinking:

alex: I like the idea. We need to nail the state machine though. Proposal: RESERVED -> COMMIT (on first write/fault) -> PINNED. RESERVED means accounted but not physical backing. COMMIT pins physical pages. How do we handle migration/offload when in RESERVED?

tomas: Can we avoid a new durable state machine by piggybacking on the existing reservation token system? e.g., reserve just increments quota and attaches a frag_hint; actual residency decisions are left to the evictor. That keeps interfaces small. :eyes:

jin: NUMA/offload concern: if RESERVED allocations count against tenant quotas but aren't resident, we risk starving hosts if everyone reserves and never commits. We should separate "quota_reserved" vs "resident_quota" and only charge resident_quota to the eviction/admission path. Otherwise offload will see artificial pressure.

maria: good point. My thought: `lazy_reserve(range, opts)` would take opts = {deadline_ms, frag_tolerance, prefault_hint}. semantics: we only charge resident_quota when COMMIT happens (first access). RESERVED does count against a lightweight reservation budget that is cheaper and has separate limits. keepable across microbatches for X ms by default.

lisa: measurement note: our offline microbench (seq_len=1024, batch=8 small tensors) shows 18% lower fragmentation when we delay backing for ~12ms. But tail latency spikes if commit causes synchronous pagefaults on hot paths. need async commit path + fast path fallback.

alex: async commit + on-path hedging: when commit would block, we do: 1) start async memcpy/prefetch 2) run fastpath partial compute that tolerates missing pages (e.g., recompute trivial ops) 3) fallback to blocking commit if not ready after Y ms. pseudo:```text
if (fault && async_ok) { start_async_commit(); continue; if (!ready_by_deadline) blocking_commit(); }```

sre-jen: crash/leak semantics: RESERVED allocations that persist across worker crash = risk. need GC/cleanup on process exit and also an expiration TTL. Also telemetry: how many RESERVED never COMMIT. Alert if >10% over 1h.

raj: product POV: expose `reserved_count`, `reserved_never_committed_ratio`, and `avg_commit_latency` per-tenant in console. customers want knobs: max_reserved_budget & reserved_timeout_ms. Also allow per-route override.

jin: offload interplay: offloader should be allowed to evict RESERVED pages w/o paying pin/unpin cost; but eviction order should prefer RESERVED over PINNED. For correctness, we must make sure that when a RESERVED page is evicted we don't lose the reservation token — only the resident mapping. evictor needs a flag.

maria: agree. Implementation sketch: add a tiny flag in page meta `is_reserved_hint` and a per-tenant reserve ledger. eviction Priority: PINNED -> COMMITTED (recently used) -> RESERVED. Also add compact-trigger when reserved fragmentation crosses threshold.

alex: microbench numbers i ran this morning (toy driver):
- baseline eager: alloc+commit per small-tensor = 4.8ms total
- lazy_reserve + async commit: alloc (reserve) = 0.6ms, commit avg = 1.2ms async, tail 99.9 = 8.9ms if blocking
So net win for short-lived allocations but need to control tail.

lisa: we should surface a "commit hedging" knob that controls the hedging strategy (none / async+fallback / always-prefault). Default async+fallback.

maria: API proposal (very rough):```c
// lightweight reservation: cheap, non-resident, expires
alloc_token_t lazy_reserve(size_t bytes, reserve_opts_t opts);

// commit on access (library/hardware triggers), but can be forced
int lazy_commit(alloc_token_t t); // blocking
int lazy_try_commit_async(alloc_token_t t, commit_cb cb);

// cancel/expire
void lazy_release(alloc_token_t t);
```

tomas: Implementation concern: changing alloc API surface is heavy. Could we implement lazy_reserve as a wrapper that returns a normal allocation handle but with an internal shadow that only materializes pages on-demand? E.g., `alloc_flags |= ALLOC_LAZY` with the same ABI. That reduces churn but complicates bookkeeping.

maria: wrapper approach is attractive for rollout. We can add `ALLOC_LAZY` flag and route it through existing alloc path; internally we set `is_reserved_hint` and ledger. No public ABI change for consumers. We still need new admin metrics and eviction ordering.

raj: rollout plan idea: default enable ALLOC_LAZY only for dedicated/dedicated-dev customers behind feature flag. Then evaluate tail latencies and fragmentation savings before wider roll. Can we add experiment tags in the console?

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature-flag/lazy-reserve-toggle -> staging on ci-1234 :rocket:

lisa: one more note — compaction: reserved-but-never-committed allocations should be prime candidates for compaction because they add virtual fragmentation. compactor should be aware of reservation age.

alex: ok next steps i propose:
1) implement `ALLOC_LAZY` flag as internal wrapper (low risk)
2) add reserved ledger + per-tenant budget + TTL enforcement
3) async commit path + hedging fallback (configurable)
4) telemetry in console for reserved metrics + alerts
5) small canary behind dedicated feature flag

maria: thanks all — i'll draft a short followup RFC with the API sketch, failure modes, and the canary plan. tagging @tomas @jin for implementation volunteers. :thumbsup:
